evidence: The methods section explicitly describes the counterfactual scenario.

claim: Given improvements in coverage over time, there is a general decline in the mean number of predicted deaths due to the 10 VIMC pathogens in each of the 112 countries.
source: We find that given these improvements in coverage over time, there is a general decline in the mean number of predicted deaths due to the 10 VIMC pathogens in each of the 112 countries.
evidence: The results section presents this finding from the study's modeling.

claim: The total burden caused by these diseases disproportionately lies within the WHO African region.
source: Notably, the total burden caused by these diseases disproportionately lies within the WHO African region where the greatest decline in burden is predicted (Figure 1 and Appendix 5—figure 4).
evidence: The results section presents this finding with reference to Figure 1 and Appendix 5—figure 4.

claim: Mortality related to Hib, measles, Rota, rubella, and PCV is mostly focused in children under-5.
source: The ages at which the greatest mortality risks are faced varies across the pathogens with mortality related to Hib, measles, Rota, rubella, and PCV mostly focused in children under-5 (Appendix 5—figure 5 shows a corresponding decline in deaths in the under-5s when vaccination occurs).
evidence: The results section presents this finding with reference to Appendix 5—figure 5.

claim: Mortality attributable to HepB and HPV is focused in those over 40.
source: Mortality attributable to HepB and HPV is focused in those over 40, and for YF, MenA and JE this is focused in those under 30 (due to natural immunity acquired with age in older adults).
evidence: The results section presents this finding from the study's modeling.

claim: For YF, MenA and JE, mortality is focused in those under 30 due to natural immunity acquired with age in older adults.
source: Mortality attributable to HepB and HPV is focused in those over 40, and for YF, MenA and JE this is focused in those under 30 (due to natural immunity acquired with age in older adults).
evidence: The results section presents this finding from the study's modeling with an explanation.

claim: In April 2020, Gavi estimated that at least 13.5 million people may have missed vaccinations with disruption likely to continue.
source: Disruptions to health services caused by the COVID-19 pandemic have been an example of such disruption and in April 2020, Gavi estimated that at least 13.5 million people may have missed vaccinations with disruption likely to continue (Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, 2020).
evidence: The discussion section cites Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, 2020 for this estimate.

claim: Chandir et al., 2020 estimated that one in every two children in Sindh province, Pakistan have missed their routine vaccinations during lockdown associated with the pandemic.
source: Similarly, Chandir et al., 2020 estimated that one in every two children in Sindh province, Pakistan have missed their routine vaccinations during lockdown associated with the pandemic.
evidence: The discussion section cites Chandir et al., 2020 for this estimate.

claim: Disruption in immunisation might be partially offset by decreased disease transmission due to NPIs implemented to help control COVID-19, as has been shown for influenza and norovirus.
source: However, this disruption in immunisation might be partially offset by decreased disease transmission due to NPIs implemented to help control COVID-19, as has been shown for influenza and norovirus (Jones, 2020; Kraay et al., 2020).
evidence: The discussion section cites Jones, 2020 and Kraay et al., 2020 for evidence of this effect.

claim: Abbas et al., 2020a assessed the benefit of continuing routine childhood immunisation in Africa given the ongoing pandemic and found the benefits outweighed the costs with 84 child deaths averted by sustained childhood immunisation per 1 excess COVID-19 death.
source: Abbas et al., 2020a assessed the benefit of continuing routine childhood immunisation in Africa given the ongoing pandemic. They found the benefits outweighed the costs with 84 (95% uncertainty interval 14-267) child deaths averted by sustained childhood immunisation per 1 excess COVID-19 death even with the risks associated with vaccination clinic visits.
evidence: The discussion section cites Abbas et al., 2020a for this finding.

claim: The VIMC Working Group on COVID-19 Impact on VPDs found that short-term disruption will likely increase burden for yellow fever and measles as they affect younger age groups and are prone to outbreaks.
source: The VIMC Working Group on COVID-19 Impact on VPDs analysed the effect of COVID-19 disruption on measles, MenA and YF through modelling scenarios of routine immunisation service disruptions and mass vaccination campaign suspensions in a subset of countries (Gaythorpe et al., 2021b). They found that the nature of the disease affects the impact of vaccination activity disruption; for example, YF and measles affect younger age groups and are prone to outbreaks, thus short-term disruption will likely increase burden.
evidence: The discussion section cites Gaythorpe et al., 2021b for this finding.

claim: Protection afforded by previous vaccination activities for MenA can mitigate the short-term effects due to COVID-19 disruption.
source: However, protection afforded by previous vaccination activities for MenA can mitigate the short-term effects due to COVID-19 disruption.
evidence: The discussion section presents this finding from the VIMC Working Group study.

claim: Standardised, national-level, age-stratified demographic data was provided to all modellers from the 2019 United Nations World Population Prospects (UNWPP) for years 2000 to 2100.
source: Standardised, national-level, age-stratified demographic data was provided to all modellers from the 2019 United Nations World Population Prospects (UNWPP) for years 2000 to 2100 (World Population Prospects, 2019).
evidence: The methods section cites World Population Prospects, 2019 as the data source.

claim: Each modelling group provided 200 samples of their burden estimates for each year, vaccination scenario, and country constructed from the probabilistic ranges of their model parameters.
source: For every pathogen, the modelling teams were asked to provide 200 samples of their burden estimates for each year, vaccination scenario, and country constructed from the probabilistic ranges of their model parameters.
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes the sampling methodology.

claim: The same randomly sampled sets of parameters were used for the no vaccination and with vaccination model runs allowing the direct comparison of the estimates.
source: The same randomly sampled sets of parameters were used for the no vaccination and with vaccination model runs allowing the direct comparison of the estimates.
evidence: The methods section explicitly describes this methodological approach.

claim: DALYs measure the years of healthy life lost due to premature death and disability from the disease, and are the sum of years of life lost (YLLs) through premature mortality and years lived with disability (YLDs).
source: DALYs measure the years of healthy life lost due to premature death and disability from the disease, and are the sum of years of life lost (YLLs) through premature mortality and years lived with disability (YLDs).
evidence: The methods section explicitly defines DALYs.

claim: No discounting or weighting was applied in the calculation of DALYs.

claim: For rubella, only disease burden from congenital rubella syndrome (CRS) was included.

evidence: The methods section explicitly states this modeling choice.

claim: Most of the mortality reduction from measles is attributable to routine MCV1, for which procurement is not directly funded by Gavi.
source: Most of the mortality reduction from measles is attributable to routine MCV1, for which procurement is not directly funded by Gavi.
evidence: The results section presents this finding from the study's analysis.

claim: As measles-related mortality is focused in children under-5, a large number of DALYs are averted when immunising against this disease.
source: As measles-related mortality is focused in children under-5, a large number of DALYs are averted when immunising against this disease.
evidence: The results section presents this inference from the study's findings.

claim: As HepB-attributable deaths are primarily focused in those over 40 years of age, there are fewer YLLs but morbidity contributes to higher numbers of YLDs.

claim: When attributing vaccine impact to the year of vaccination and aggregating mortality across all 10 pathogens, double counting is not adjusted for.
source: When attributing vaccine impact to the year of vaccination, and aggregating mortality across all 10 pathogens, we do not adjust for double counting, thereby counting an individual's death more than once when mortality arises by more than one pathogen (Li et al., 2019).
evidence: The methods section explicitly states this methodological choice with a citation.

claim: Double counting is accounted for when aggregating vaccine impact over a calendar year and birth cohort.

claim: The study represents the largest assessment of vaccine impact before COVID-19-related disruptions.
